characters: The narrator (Dr. Watson, who is not named in the excerpt) waits for Holmes at Baker Street
Sherlock Holmes returns disguised as a drunken groom and tells Watson about his morning

Irene Adler, Godfrey Norton and the ostlers appear only in Holmes's account, not in the room
characters_main: Names Sherlock Holmes as the most important character (Watson or Irene Adler acceptable if well justified)

summary: The narrator waits at Baker Street and Holmes returns around four o'clock disguised as a drunken groom, then changes and laughs about his morning
Holmes spent the morning disguised as an out-of-work groom to gather information about Miss Irene Adler
He examined Briony Lodge closely, noting the sitting-room windows and that the passage window can be reached from the coach-house roof
From the ostlers in the mews he learned that Adler lives quietly, sings at concerts, and has one frequent visitor, Mr. Godfrey Norton of the Inner Temple
